faqs.answer: Yes. Both are fully open source. GAIA is self-hostable via Docker, and OMI publishes its code for inspection and self-hosting.
faqs.question: Are GAIA and OMI both open source?

faqs.answer: No. GAIA works with your existing phone and laptop across web, desktop, mobile, and messaging apps. No wearable required.
faqs.question: Do I need OMI hardware to use GAIA?

intro: OMI deserves credit: an open-source pendant in a category of closed microphones is a brave product. It listens, records, and makes your day searchable. But recall is where it stops. Nobody ever cleared their inbox by remembering it better. GAIA shares OMI's open-source values and finishes the job: it takes context and acts on it, drafting the follow-up, creating the task, moving the meeting. Two open products, two different halves of the problem.
